title: Resource Health Events

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `mscs:azure:audit` events with `category.value="ResourceHealth"` into `index=azure`. Confirm UC-4.2.11 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `mscs:azure:audit` traffic without `category.value="ResourceHealth"`. Confirm UC-4.2.11 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=azure` sourcetype=`mscs:azure:audit` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.

description: UC-4.2.11 — Resource Health Events: queries Microsoft Azure `mscs:azure:audit` for search criteria `category.value="ResourceHealth"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for availability review and change validation.

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` with the modular input for `mscs:azure:audit`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Resource Health events flow through the Activity Log. Monitor for Unavailable and Degraded statuses. Correlate with your application health metrics to distinguish Azure platform issues from your own problems.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:audit" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:audit" category.value="ResourceHealth"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.11_resource_health_events_11"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `mscs:azure:audit` in `index=azure` to detect resource health events. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_11_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Status panel per resource type, Table, Timeline..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of resource health events so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
